resources.string: CellWatch is a FCC Challenge app. You can collect measurements to send to the FCC to show that your coverage doesn’t meet the minimum standards, or take measurements to test speeds for yourself.
¿Prefiere español? Se puede cambiar el idioma en los ajustes del dispositivo.

To formally challenge a provider’s performance claims, you need to take several measurements within a geographic area and submit them to the FCC, the U.S. government agency that regulates telecommunications.
Our app helps consumers take these measurements and automatically submits them to the FCC.

A challenge to a provider’s coverage claims is specific to a geographic area. The FCC has used a hexagonal tiling system to define regions. By collecting several measurements within one hexagonal region, a consumer can prove that the region does not have good mobile Internet performance, despite what their cell carrier may claim.
Our app shows two layers of hexagonal regions: each large hexagonal region contains seven (7) child hexagons.
Challenges are for the larger hexagons, and you must take measurements within a specific number of child hexagons to count as a challenge.
The data you collect with CellWatch will be shared with the public, including the general location and time of your measurements.
Your CellWatch data may also be used for research purposes.
Please read our privacy policy for details.
Would you like to work towards a formal FCC challenge? You can update this later in the app settings.
Measurements will be sent to the FCC as challenge data. The FCC may make public your exact GPS location, provider, and other relevant details. Data will also be shared with CellWatch.
Measurements will not be sent to the FCC but will be shared with CellWatch.
If you would like to work toward an official FCC challenge, this information must be submitted to the FCC with your measurements.
I acknowledge that my service provider may share necessary customer-specific information with the FCC (such as IP address and service plan details).

In order to take measurements, we need the following permissions:

1. Location, to know where measurements are taken.

2. Phone calls, to gather information about your cellular connection. We will never make phone calls.
When ready, click \"Allow\" when prompted. You can update these permissions later in your device\'s settings.
